meta.topic: 复变基础：复数、复平面、三角形式与棣莫弗定理、复变函数、极限与连续、解析函数、柯西-黎曼方程

zh: 规定 $i^2=-1$，形如 $z=x+iy$（$x,y\in\mathbb R$）的数称为复数，其中 $x=\operatorname{Re}z$ 是实部、$y=\operatorname{Im}z$ 是虚部。两个复数相等当且仅当实部与虚部分别相等，即 $x_1+iy_1=x_2+iy_2\iff x_1=x_2$ 且 $y_1=y_2$；因此一个复等式等价于两个实等式。$y=0$ 时 $z$ 为实数，$x=0$ 且 $y\ne0$ 时为纯虚数。加法按分量进行，乘法按多项式展开并利用 $i^2=-1$：$$(a+bi)(c+di)=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i.$$

复数对加、减、乘、除（除数非零）封闭，构成数域 $\mathbb C$，且 $\mathbb R\subset\mathbb C$。关键是每个非零复数有倒数：由 $(a+bi)(a-bi)=a^2+b^2\ne0$ 得 $$(a+bi)^{-1}=\frac{a-bi}{a^2+b^2}.$$ 于是除法可化为乘法：$$\frac{a+bi}{c+di}=\frac{(a+bi)(c-di)}{c^2+d^2}\quad(c+di\ne0).$$ 这里分母 $c^2+d^2>0$，所以结果唯一；加乘满足交换律、结合律与分配律，$0$、$1$ 分别为零元与单位元。

共轭复数定义为 $\bar z=x-iy$，几何上是关于实轴的对称点。共轭是对合：$\overline{\bar z}=z$；并且与四则运算相容：$$\overline{z_1\pm z_2}=\bar z_1\pm\bar z_2,\quad \overline{z_1z_2}=\bar z_1\bar z_2,\quad \overline{\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)}=\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2}\ (z_2\ne0).$$ 例如乘积式可由 $(x_1+iy_1)(x_2+iy_2)$ 展开后逐项变号验证。由此可提取实部与虚部：$$\operatorname{Re}z=\frac{z+\bar z}{2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}z=\frac{z-\bar z}{2i}.$$ 特别地，$z\in\mathbb R\iff z=\bar z$，$z$ 为非零纯虚数 $\iff \bar z=-z$。

模定义为 $|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\ge0$，它等于点 $z$ 到原点的距离。由定义直接得到 $$z\bar z=(x+iy)(x-iy)=x^2+y^2=|z|^2,$$ 所以当 $z\ne0$ 时 $z^{-1}=\bar z/|z|^2$。模对乘法可拆：$$\begin{aligned}|z_1z_2|^2&=(z_1z_2)\overline{(z_1z_2)}\\&=z_1z_2\bar z_1\bar z_2=|z_1|^2|z_2|^2,\end{aligned}$$ 两边开方得 $|z_1z_2|=|z_1||z_2|$；再由 $z_1=(z_1/z_2)z_2$ 得 $|z_1/z_2|=|z_1|/|z_2|$（$z_2\ne0$）。同时 $|\bar z|=|z|$。

对任意 $z_1,z_2$，有 $$\begin{aligned}|z_1+z_2|^2&=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2\\&\quad+2\operatorname{Re}(z_1\bar z_2).\end{aligned}$$ 由 $\operatorname{Re}w\le|w|$ 得 $\operatorname{Re}(z_1\bar z_2)\le|z_1||z_2|$，故 $$|z_1+z_2|^2\le(|z_1|+|z_2|)^2,$$ 即三角不等式 $|z_1+z_2|\le|z_1|+|z_2|$。等号当且仅当 $z_1\bar z_2$ 为非负实数，即两向量同向（或其中一个为零）。由 $|z_1|=|(z_1-z_2)+z_2|\le|z_1-z_2|+|z_2|$ 得 $|z_1|-|z_2|\le|z_1-z_2|$；再交换 $z_1,z_2$ 得 $|z_2|-|z_1|\le|z_1-z_2|$，合并即得反向不等式 $\bigl||z_1|-|z_2|\bigr|\le|z_1-z_2|$。

复数不能比较大小：若存在与加法、乘法相容的全序，则非零元素的平方应为正，于是 $1=1^2>0$；但 $i^2=-1$ 也应为正，从而 $-1>0$，相加得 $0>1$，与 $1>0$ 矛盾。因此 $z>0$ 一类写法没有意义，复数的大小只能用模来度量。代数的补偿是：$\mathbb C$ 是代数闭域，任一 $n\ge1$ 次复系数多项式在 $\mathbb C$ 中恰有 $n$ 个根（按重数计）；几何上 $z\leftrightarrow(x,y)$ 把复数变成平面向量，加法就是平行四边形法则，这为复平面与复变函数提供了舞台。
en: Set $i^2=-1$. A number of the form $z=x+iy$ with $x,y\in\mathbb R$ is a complex number, with real part $x=\operatorname{Re}z$ and imaginary part $y=\operatorname{Im}z$. Two complex numbers are equal exactly when their real and imaginary parts are equal: $x_1+iy_1=x_2+iy_2$ iff $x_1=x_2$ and $y_1=y_2$. Thus one complex equation is two real equations. If $y=0$, $z$ is real; if $x=0$ and $y\ne0$, it is purely imaginary. Addition is componentwise, and multiplication follows polynomial rules with $i^2=-1$: $$(a+bi)(c+di)=(ac-bd)+(ad+bc)i.$$

The complex numbers are closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication and division by nonzero elements, forming the field $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R\subset\mathbb C$. The key point is that every nonzero complex number has a reciprocal: from $(a+bi)(a-bi)=a^2+b^2\ne0$, $$(a+bi)^{-1}=\frac{a-bi}{a^2+b^2}.$$ Hence division reduces to multiplication: $$\frac{a+bi}{c+di}=\frac{(a+bi)(c-di)}{c^2+d^2}\quad(c+di\ne0).$$ The denominator $c^2+d^2>0$, so the result is unique; addition and multiplication are commutative, associative and distributive, with neutral elements $0$ and $1$.

The conjugate is $\bar z=x-iy$; geometrically it is the reflection of $z$ in the real axis. Conjugation is an involution, $\overline{\bar z}=z$, and is compatible with the four operations: $$\overline{z_1\pm z_2}=\bar z_1\pm\bar z_2,\quad \overline{z_1z_2}=\bar z_1\bar z_2,\quad \overline{\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)}=\frac{\bar z_1}{\bar z_2}\ (z_2\ne0).$$ For instance, the product identity follows by expanding $(x_1+iy_1)(x_2+iy_2)$ and reversing the sign of every imaginary term. This yields the real and imaginary parts: $$\operatorname{Re}z=\frac{z+\bar z}{2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}z=\frac{z-\bar z}{2i}.$$ In particular, $z\in\mathbb R$ iff $z=\bar z$, and $z$ is nonzero purely imaginary iff $\bar z=-z$.

The modulus is $|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\ge0$, the distance from $z$ to the origin. By definition, $$z\bar z=(x+iy)(x-iy)=x^2+y^2=|z|^2,$$ so for $z\ne0$, $z^{-1}=\bar z/|z|^2$. The modulus is multiplicative: $$\begin{aligned}|z_1z_2|^2&=(z_1z_2)\overline{(z_1z_2)}\\&=z_1z_2\bar z_1\bar z_2=|z_1|^2|z_2|^2.\end{aligned}$$ Taking square roots gives $|z_1z_2|=|z_1||z_2|$; then $z_1=(z_1/z_2)z_2$ gives $|z_1/z_2|=|z_1|/|z_2|$ for $z_2\ne0$. Also $|\bar z|=|z|$.

For any $z_1,z_2$, $$\begin{aligned}|z_1+z_2|^2&=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2\\&\quad+2\operatorname{Re}(z_1\bar z_2).\end{aligned}$$ Since $\operatorname{Re}w\le|w|$, we have $\operatorname{Re}(z_1\bar z_2)\le|z_1||z_2|$, hence $$|z_1+z_2|^2\le(|z_1|+|z_2|)^2,$$ that is, the triangle inequality $|z_1+z_2|\le|z_1|+|z_2|$. Equality holds exactly when $z_1\bar z_2$ is a nonnegative real number, i.e. the two vectors point in the same direction (or one of them is zero). From $|z_1|=|(z_1-z_2)+z_2|\le|z_1-z_2|+|z_2|$ we get $|z_1|-|z_2|\le|z_1-z_2|$; swapping $z_1,z_2$ gives the opposite inequality, and combining yields the reverse triangle inequality $\bigl||z_1|-|z_2|\bigr|\le|z_1-z_2|$.

Complex numbers cannot be ordered: if a total order compatible with addition and multiplication existed, the square of every nonzero element would be positive, so $1=1^2>0$; but $i^2=-1$ would also be positive, hence $-1>0$, and adding gives $0>1$, contradicting $1>0$. Thus expressions such as $z>0$ are meaningless, and size can be measured only by the modulus. Algebraically, $\mathbb C$ is algebraically closed: every polynomial of degree $n\ge1$ with complex coefficients has exactly $n$ roots in $\mathbb C$, counted with multiplicity. Geometrically, $z\leftrightarrow(x,y)$ turns complex numbers into plane vectors, with addition given by the parallelogram law, preparing the ground for the complex plane and complex functions.

zh: 取平面直角坐标系，横轴为实轴、纵轴为虚轴，复数 $z=x+iy$ 对应点 $(x,y)$，也对应从原点出发的向量 $\overrightarrow{OZ}$。这种一一对应使复数的加法就是向量加法：$(x_1,y_1)+(x_2,y_2)=(x_1+x_2,y_1+y_2)$。两点间距离为 $$|z_1-z_2|=\sqrt{(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2},$$ 例如 $|z|=|z-0|$ 是点 $z$ 到原点的距离。

对 $z\ne0$，模 $r=|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}>0$；从正实轴逆时针转到向量 $z$ 的角 $\theta$ 称为辐角，满足 $$\cos\theta=\frac{x}{r},\qquad \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}.$$ 辐角不唯一：若 $\theta$ 是一个辐角，则 $\theta+2k\pi$（$k\in\mathbb Z$）都是；记多值函数为 $\operatorname{Arg}z$。把辐角限制在 $(-\pi,\pi]$ 内得到主值 $\arg z$，于是 $\operatorname{Arg}z=\arg z+2k\pi$。$z=0$ 的模为零，辐角无意义；两个非零复数相等当且仅当模相等且辐角相差 $2\pi$ 的整数倍。

由 $x=r\cos\theta$、$y=r\sin\theta$ 得三角形式 $$z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta).$$ 再由欧拉公式 $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$，得到指数形式 $$z=re^{i\theta}.$$ 互化时先算 $r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$，再由 $\cos\theta=x/r$、$\sin\theta=y/r$ 的符号确定象限；只用 $\tan\theta=y/x$ 会把角定到相差 $\pi$ 的两个候选中。例如 $z=-1+\sqrt{3}\,i$ 有 $r=2$，位于第二象限，故 $\arg z=2\pi/3$，即 $z=2e^{2\pi i/3}$。

设 $z_1=r_1e^{i\theta_1}$、$z_2=r_2e^{i\theta_2}$。由指数律与三角和角公式，$$\begin{aligned}z_1z_2&=r_1r_2e^{i(\theta_1+\theta_2)},\\ \frac{z_1}{z_2}&=\frac{r_1}{r_2}e^{i(\theta_1-\theta_2)}\quad(z_2\ne0).\end{aligned}$$ 即乘法「模相乘、辐角相加」，除法「模相除、辐角相减」。几何上，乘以 $z_2$ 把 $z_1$ 的向量绕原点逆时针旋转 $\theta_2$，再把长度伸缩 $r_2$ 倍；特别地乘 $i=e^{i\pi/2}$ 是逆时针旋转 $90^\circ$，乘 $-1=e^{i\pi}$ 是旋转 $180^\circ$。除以 $z_2$ 则反向旋转，并按 $1/|z_2|$ 伸缩（$|z_2|>1$ 时缩短，$0<|z_2|<1$ 时放大，$|z_2|=1$ 时长度不变）。

共轭 $\bar z=x-iy$ 对应关于实轴的对称点，因此 $|\bar z|=|z|$，且 $\operatorname{Arg}\bar z=-\operatorname{Arg}z$（理解为辐角集合）。复平面上的常见轨迹可直接用模与辐角表示：$|z-z_0|=R$ 是以 $z_0$ 为圆心、$R$ 为半径的圆周；$|z-z_0|<R$ 是圆盘；$\arg(z-z_0)=\alpha$ 是从 $z_0$ 出发、方向角为 $\alpha$ 的射线（不含 $z_0$）。例如 $|z-1|=|z+i|$ 化为 $(x-1)^2+y^2=x^2+(y+1)^2$，即 $y=-x$，是端点 $1$ 与 $-i$ 所连线段的垂直平分线。

由三角不等式，对任意三点 $z_1,z_2,z_3$ 有 $$|z_1-z_3|\le|z_1-z_2|+|z_2-z_3|,$$ 几何上就是三角形两边之和不小于第三边；等号当且仅当三点共线且 $z_2$ 位于 $z_1,z_3$ 之间（允许端点重合）。于是 $d(z,w)=|z-w|$ 是复平面上的距离，$z_n\to z$ 等价于实部、虚部分别收敛。复平面因此既是代数对象（数域），又是度量空间，这两重身份贯穿复变函数始终。
en: Take rectangular coordinates in the plane, with the real axis horizontal and the imaginary axis vertical. The complex number $z=x+iy$ corresponds to the point $(x,y)$ and to the vector $\overrightarrow{OZ}$ from the origin. This one-to-one correspondence makes addition the usual vector addition: $(x_1,y_1)+(x_2,y_2)=(x_1+x_2,y_1+y_2)$. The distance between two points is $$|z_1-z_2|=\sqrt{(x_1-x_2)^2+(y_1-y_2)^2},$$ so for example $|z|=|z-0|$ is the distance from $z$ to the origin.

For $z\ne0$, the modulus is $r=|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}>0$, and the angle $\theta$ from the positive real axis counterclockwise to the vector $z$ is an argument, characterized by $$\cos\theta=\frac{x}{r},\qquad \sin\theta=\frac{y}{r}.$$ Arguments are not unique: if $\theta$ is one, so is $\theta+2k\pi$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$; the multivalued function is $\operatorname{Arg}z$. Restricting to $(-\pi,\pi]$ gives the principal value $\arg z$, so $\operatorname{Arg}z=\arg z+2k\pi$. The number $z=0$ has modulus zero and no argument; two nonzero complex numbers are equal iff their moduli agree and their arguments differ by an integer multiple of $2\pi$.

From $x=r\cos\theta$ and $y=r\sin\theta$ we obtain the trigonometric form $$z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta).$$ Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ then gives the exponential form $$z=re^{i\theta}.$$ To convert, first compute $r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$, then determine the quadrant from the signs of $\cos\theta=x/r$ and $\sin\theta=y/r$; using only $\tan\theta=y/x$ leaves two candidates differing by $\pi$. For example, $z=-1+\sqrt{3}\,i$ has $r=2$ and lies in the second quadrant, so $\arg z=2\pi/3$ and $z=2e^{2\pi i/3}$.

Let $z_1=r_1e^{i\theta_1}$ and $z_2=r_2e^{i\theta_2}$. By the exponential law and the addition formulas for sine and cosine, $$\begin{aligned}z_1z_2&=r_1r_2e^{i(\theta_1+\theta_2)},\\ \frac{z_1}{z_2}&=\frac{r_1}{r_2}e^{i(\theta_1-\theta_2)}\quad(z_2\ne0).\end{aligned}$$ That is, multiplication multiplies moduli and adds arguments, while division divides moduli and subtracts arguments. Geometrically, multiplying $z_1$ by $z_2$ rotates its vector counterclockwise through $\theta_2$ and scales its length by $r_2$; in particular multiplication by $i=e^{i\pi/2}$ is a counterclockwise quarter-turn, and by $-1=e^{i\pi}$ a half-turn. Division rotates back and scales by $1/|z_2|$ (shrinking for $|z_2|>1$, enlarging for $0<|z_2|<1$, and preserving length for $|z_2|=1$).

The conjugate $\bar z=x-iy$ corresponds to reflection in the real axis, so $|\bar z|=|z|$ and $\operatorname{Arg}\bar z=-\operatorname{Arg}z$ (as sets of arguments). Common loci in the complex plane have immediate modulus-argument descriptions: $|z-z_0|=R$ is the circle with centre $z_0$ and radius $R$; $|z-z_0|<R$ is its interior; $\arg(z-z_0)=\alpha$ is the ray from $z_0$ in direction $\alpha$, with $z_0$ removed. For instance, $|z-1|=|z+i|$ becomes $(x-1)^2+y^2=x^2+(y+1)^2$, i.e. $y=-x$, the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $1$ and $-i$.

The triangle inequality gives, for any three points $z_1,z_2,z_3$, $$|z_1-z_3|\le|z_1-z_2|+|z_2-z_3|,$$ which is the geometric statement that the sum of two sides of a triangle is at least the third; equality holds iff the three points are collinear with $z_2$ between $z_1$ and $z_3$ (endpoints may coincide). Hence $d(z,w)=|z-w|$ is a distance on the complex plane, and $z_n\to z$ iff the real and imaginary parts converge separately. The complex plane is thus both an algebraic object (a field) and a metric space, a duality that runs through all of complex analysis.

zh: 设 $z=a+bi\ne0$，令 $r=|z|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}>0$。选取 $\theta$ 使 $$\cos\theta=\frac{a}{r},\qquad \sin\theta=\frac{b}{r},$$ 则 $a=r\cos\theta$、$b=r\sin\theta$，于是 $$z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta).$$ 这就是三角形式。规范写法要求：$r\ge0$；括号内 $\cos$ 在前、$\sin$ 在后；两处是同一个角 $\theta$；中间用加号连接。本节点局部把非零复数的辐角主值取在 $[0,2\pi)$ 内，其他辐角为 $\theta+2k\pi$；本分支的 complex-plane 节点采用 $(-\pi,\pi]$，两者只差 $2\pi$，跨节点请使用辐角集合 $\operatorname{Arg}z$ 或显式换算。

设 $z_1=r_1(\cos\theta_1+i\sin\theta_1)$、$z_2=r_2(\cos\theta_2+i\sin\theta_2)$。展开乘积并用和角公式：$$z_1z_2=r_1r_2\bigl[\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2)+i\sin(\theta_1+\theta_2)\bigr],$$ 因为实部为 $\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2-\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2$，虚部为 $\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2+\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2$。当 $z_2\ne0$ 时，同法（或对 $z_2$ 取倒数）得 $$\frac{z_1}{z_2}=\frac{r_1}{r_2}\bigl[\cos(\theta_1-\theta_2)+i\sin(\theta_1-\theta_2)\bigr].$$ 角的和差若超出主值区间，要加减 $2k\pi$ 化回 $[0,2\pi)$。

乘法公式的几何意义是旋转加伸缩：把 $z_1$ 的向量绕原点逆时针旋转 $\theta_2$，长度变为 $r_2$ 倍，就得到 $z_1z_2$。特别地，$i=\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{2}$，乘以 $i$ 是逆时针旋转 $90^\circ$ 且模不变；乘以 $-1=\cos\pi+i\sin\pi$ 是旋转 $180^\circ$。除法是乘法的逆：旋转 $-\theta_2$、伸缩 $1/r_2$。因此三角形式把「乘除」化为「模与角的加减」，比代数形式展开更直接。

棣莫弗定理：对 $n\in\mathbb N^*$，$$\bigl[r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)\bigr]^n=r^n(\cos n\theta+i\sin n\theta).$$ 证明用归纳法。$n=1$ 时两边相同。若 $n$ 时成立，则再乘一次 $z$，由乘法公式：$$z^{n+1}=r^n r\bigl[\cos(n\theta+\theta)+i\sin(n\theta+\theta)\bigr],$$ 即 $r^{n+1}\bigl[\cos((n+1)\theta)+i\sin((n+1)\theta)\bigr]$，归纳完成。当 $r\ne0$ 时，对负整数 $n=-m$ 也有 $z^{-m}=1/z^m=r^{-m}\bigl(\cos(-m\theta)+i\sin(-m\theta)\bigr)$。

应用一例：$1+i=\sqrt2\bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\bigr)$，故 $$\begin{aligned}(1+i)^6&=(\sqrt2)^6\left(\cos\frac{6\pi}{4}+i\sin\frac{6\pi}{4}\right)\\&=8\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2}+i\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-8i.\end{aligned}$$ 另一类应用是比较实部与虚部：由 $(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)^3=\cos3\theta+i\sin3\theta$，左边展开为 $\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta+i(3\cos^2\theta\sin\theta-\sin^3\theta)$，于是 $$\begin{aligned}\cos3\theta&=\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta=4\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta,\\ \sin3\theta&=3\cos^2\theta\sin\theta-\sin^3\theta=3\sin\theta-4\sin^3\theta.\end{aligned}$$ 这把三角恒等式化成了复数乘方。

互化与运算中最容易出错的是形式不规范。例如 $$-2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=2\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}\right),$$ $$2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}-i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=2\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right),$$ 必须先化成 $r\ge0$、$\cos$ 与 $\sin$ 同角且以加号相连，才能套用乘除与棣莫弗公式。定角时必须结合点 $(a,b)$ 的象限核对 $\cos\theta=a/r$、$\sin\theta=b/r$ 的符号；$z=0$ 没有辐角，不能写成三角形式。两个非零复数相等，当且仅当模相等且辐角相差 $2\pi$ 的整数倍。
en: Let $z=a+bi\ne0$ and set $r=|z|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}>0$. Choose $\theta$ such that $$\cos\theta=\frac{a}{r},\qquad \sin\theta=\frac{b}{r}.$$ Then $a=r\cos\theta$ and $b=r\sin\theta$, hence $$z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta).$$ This is the trigonometric form. A standard expression requires: $r\ge0$; cosine first and sine second inside the bracket; the same angle $\theta$ in both; and a plus sign between them. In this topic the principal argument is taken locally in $[0,2\pi)$, with all other arguments $\theta+2k\pi$; the complex-plane topic uses $(-\pi,\pi]$, differing by $2\pi$, so use the argument set $\operatorname{Arg}z$ or an explicit conversion across topics.

Let $z_1=r_1(\cos\theta_1+i\sin\theta_1)$ and $z_2=r_2(\cos\theta_2+i\sin\theta_2)$. Expanding the product and using the addition formulas gives $$z_1z_2=r_1r_2\bigl[\cos(\theta_1+\theta_2)+i\sin(\theta_1+\theta_2)\bigr],$$ since the real part is $\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2-\sin\theta_1\sin\theta_2$ and the imaginary part is $\sin\theta_1\cos\theta_2+\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2$. When $z_2\ne0$, the same computation (or taking the reciprocal of $z_2$) gives $$\frac{z_1}{z_2}=\frac{r_1}{r_2}\bigl[\cos(\theta_1-\theta_2)+i\sin(\theta_1-\theta_2)\bigr].$$ If a sum or difference of angles falls outside the principal range, add or subtract $2k\pi$ to return to $[0,2\pi)$.

Geometrically, the multiplication formula is a rotation followed by a scaling: rotate the vector $z_1$ counterclockwise through $\theta_2$ and change its length by the factor $r_2$ to obtain $z_1z_2$. In particular, $i=\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{2}$, so multiplication by $i$ is a counterclockwise quarter-turn preserving the modulus, while multiplication by $-1=\cos\pi+i\sin\pi$ is a half-turn. Division is the inverse operation: rotate by $-\theta_2$ and scale by $1/r_2$. Trigonometric form thus turns multiplication and division into adding and subtracting moduli and angles, more direct than expanding algebraically.

De Moivre's theorem: for $n\in\mathbb N^*$, $$\bigl[r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)\bigr]^n=r^n(\cos n\theta+i\sin n\theta).$$ Proof by induction. For $n=1$ the two sides coincide. If the formula holds for $n$, multiply once more by $z$ and use the multiplication rule: $$z^{n+1}=r^n r\bigl[\cos(n\theta+\theta)+i\sin(n\theta+\theta)\bigr],$$ which is $r^{n+1}\bigl[\cos((n+1)\theta)+i\sin((n+1)\theta)\bigr]$, completing the induction. When $r\ne0$, for a negative integer $n=-m$ the formula also holds: $z^{-m}=1/z^m=r^{-m}\bigl(\cos(-m\theta)+i\sin(-m\theta)\bigr)$.

Example: $1+i=\sqrt2\bigl(\cos\frac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{4}\bigr)$, hence $$\begin{aligned}(1+i)^6&=(\sqrt2)^6\left(\cos\frac{6\pi}{4}+i\sin\frac{6\pi}{4}\right)\\&=8\left(\cos\frac{3\pi}{2}+i\sin\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-8i.\end{aligned}$$ Another use is comparing real and imaginary parts: from $(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)^3=\cos3\theta+i\sin3\theta$, the expansion of the left side is $\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta+i(3\cos^2\theta\sin\theta-\sin^3\theta)$, so $$\begin{aligned}\cos3\theta&=\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta=4\cos^3\theta-3\cos\theta,\\ \sin3\theta&=3\cos^2\theta\sin\theta-\sin^3\theta=3\sin\theta-4\sin^3\theta.\end{aligned}$$ This converts trigonometric identities into complex powers.

The most common errors occur with nonstandard forms. For example $$-2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=2\left(\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{4\pi}{3}\right),$$ $$2\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{3}-i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=2\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{5\pi}{3}\right).$$ They must first be rewritten with $r\ge0$, the same angle in cosine and sine, and a plus sign; only then can the product and de Moivre formulas be applied. When determining the angle, check the signs of $\cos\theta=a/r$ and $\sin\theta=b/r$ against the quadrant of $(a,b)$; $z=0$ has no argument and no trigonometric form. Two nonzero complex numbers are equal iff their moduli are equal and their arguments differ by an integer multiple of $2\pi$.

zh: 设 $G$ 是复平面上的点集（通常是区域）。若按某一法则，对每个 $z\in G$ 都有唯一确定的复数 $w$ 与之对应，则称 $w=f(z)$ 是定义在 $G$ 上的复变函数，$G$ 为定义域，全体函数值为值域。自变量与函数值都是复数，所以 $f$ 把 $z$ 平面上的点映到 $w$ 平面上的点。多数情形研究单值函数；$\operatorname{Arg}z$、$\operatorname{Ln}z$ 等多值函数要通过限制辐角范围选取单值分支。

写 $z=x+iy$、$w=u+iv$，则 $$f(z)=u(x,y)+i\,v(x,y),$$ 其中 $u=\operatorname{Re}f$、$v=\operatorname{Im}f$ 是二元实函数。因此复变函数等价于映射 $$\Phi:(x,y)\mapsto\bigl(u(x,y),v(x,y)\bigr).$$ 例如 $$z^2=(x+iy)^2=(x^2-y^2)+2xy\,i,$$ 即 $u=x^2-y^2$、$v=2xy$。复等式 $f(z)=w$ 等价于 $u(x,y)=\operatorname{Re}w$ 与 $v(x,y)=\operatorname{Im}w$ 两个实等式。

复变函数不能用一张平面图像完整表示：真正的图像在四维空间。常用画法是并排画 $z$ 平面与 $w$ 平面，用对应点或曲线表示映射；也可以只画几条特殊曲线的像来观察变换。基本变换有：$w=z+a$ 是平移；$w=az$（$a=\rho e^{i\varphi}$）是旋转 $\varphi$ 后再伸缩 $\rho$ 倍；$w=1/z=\bar z/|z|^2$ 可看成关于单位圆的反演与关于实轴的反射的复合；分式线性函数 $w=\frac{az+b}{cz+d}$（$ad-bc\ne0$）把直线与圆映为直线或圆。

以 $w=z^2$ 为例。若 $z=re^{i\theta}$，则 $$w=z^2=r^2e^{2i\theta},$$ 即模平方、辐角加倍。圆周 $|z|=2$ 映为 $|w|=4$；当 $z$ 沿圆周走一圈（$\theta$ 增加 $2\pi$）时，$w$ 沿 $|w|=4$ 走两圈。射线 $\arg z=\frac{\pi}{4}$（$r>0$）映为射线 $\arg w=\frac{\pi}{2}$。上半平面 $0<\theta<\pi$ 映为 $0<\arg w<2\pi$，即沿正实轴剪开的平面。除 $z=0$ 外，$w=z^2$ 保持两条曲线的夹角（共形），因为 $f'(z)=2z\ne0$。

映射的观点要区分像与定义域，也要注意逆映射的多值性。$w=z^2$ 没有整体单值逆：每个 $w\ne0$ 有两个原像 $\pm\sqrt w$。若把 $z$ 限制在右半平面 $\operatorname{Re}z>0$（即 $|\arg z|<\pi/2$），则 $w=z^2$ 是一一的，像为沿负实轴剪开的平面 $\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$；其逆就是主值平方根 $z=\sqrt w$。类似地，$\operatorname{Arg}z$ 多值，选定辐角范围后才有单值的 $\arg z$；对数 $\operatorname{Ln}z=\ln|z|+i\operatorname{Arg}z$ 也按同样方式取分支。
复变函数的研究重点不是任意映射，而是可微（解析）的函数。任意一对 $u,v$ 都给出一个复变函数，但只有满足柯西-黎曼方程且 $u,v$ 可微时，$f=u+iv$ 才在复意义下可导。解析函数在导数不为零处保角，因而成为平面区域之间最自然的共形映射；$z^2$、$e^z$、分式线性函数都是典型例子。后续的极限、导数、积分与级数，都是围绕「解析」这一核心条件展开的。
en: Let $G$ be a set of points in the complex plane (usually a region). If by some rule every $z\in G$ is assigned a unique complex number $w$, then $w=f(z)$ is a complex function on $G$, with domain $G$ and range the set of all values. Both variable and value are complex, so $f$ maps points of the $z$-plane to points of the $w$-plane. Most of the time we study single-valued functions; multivalued functions such as $\operatorname{Arg}z$ and $\operatorname{Ln}z$ are handled by restricting the argument to select a single-valued branch.

Write $z=x+iy$ and $w=u+iv$. Then $$f(z)=u(x,y)+i\,v(x,y),$$ where $u=\operatorname{Re}f$ and $v=\operatorname{Im}f$ are real functions of two variables. Thus a complex function is the same data as the mapping $$\Phi:(x,y)\mapsto\bigl(u(x,y),v(x,y)\bigr).$$ For example, $$z^2=(x+iy)^2=(x^2-y^2)+2xy\,i,$$ i.e. $u=x^2-y^2$ and $v=2xy$. The complex equation $f(z)=w$ is equivalent to the two real equations $u(x,y)=\operatorname{Re}w$ and $v(x,y)=\operatorname{Im}w$.

A complex function cannot be represented by a single planar graph: its genuine graph lies in four dimensions. The standard picture uses two planes, the $z$-plane and the $w$-plane, with corresponding points or curves indicating the mapping; one may also draw only the images of a few selected curves. Basic transformations include: $w=z+a$ (translation); $w=az$ with $a=\rho e^{i\varphi}$ (rotation by $\varphi$ followed by scaling by $\rho$); $w=1/z=\bar z/|z|^2$ (inversion in the unit circle composed with reflection in the real axis); and linear fractional maps $w=\frac{az+b}{cz+d}$ with $ad-bc\ne0$, which send lines and circles to lines or circles.

Take $w=z^2$. If $z=re^{i\theta}$, then $$w=z^2=r^2e^{2i\theta},$$ so the modulus is squared and the argument doubled. The circle $|z|=2$ maps to $|w|=4$; as $z$ traverses the circle once ($\theta$ increases by $2\pi$), $w$ traverses $|w|=4$ twice. The ray $\arg z=\frac{\pi}{4}$ ($r>0$) maps to the ray $\arg w=\frac{\pi}{2}$. The upper half-plane $0<\theta<\pi$ maps to $0<\arg w<2\pi$, the plane slit along the positive real axis. Except at $z=0$, $w=z^2$ preserves the angle between two curves (it is conformal), since $f'(z)=2z\ne0$.

The mapping viewpoint distinguishes images from domains and requires care with multivalued inverses. $w=z^2$ has no global single-valued inverse: every $w\ne0$ has two preimages $\pm\sqrt w$. If $z$ is restricted to the right half-plane $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ (that is, $|\arg z|<\pi/2$), then $w=z^2$ is one-to-one onto the plane slit along the negative real axis, $\mathbb C\setminus(-\infty,0]$, and its inverse is the principal square root $z=\sqrt w$. Similarly, $\operatorname{Arg}z$ is multivalued and becomes single-valued only after choosing an argument range; the logarithm $\operatorname{Ln}z=\ln|z|+i\operatorname{Arg}z$ is treated by the same branch selection.

Complex analysis focuses not on arbitrary mappings but on differentiable (analytic) functions. Any pair $u,v$ defines a complex function, but $f=u+iv$ is complex differentiable only when $u,v$ are differentiable and satisfy the Cauchy–Riemann equations. Where its derivative is nonzero, an analytic function is conformal, which makes it the natural map between plane regions; $z^2$, $e^z$ and linear fractional maps are typical examples. Limits, derivatives, integrals and series in the subject are all built around the single central condition of analyticity.

zh: 设 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 的某去心邻域内有定义。若存在复数 $A$，使得对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，存在 $\delta>0$，当 $0<|z-z_0|<\delta$ 时都有 $|f(z)-A|<\varepsilon$，则称 $$\lim_{z\to z_0}f(z)=A.$$ 与实变量不同，$0<|z-z_0|<\delta$ 不区分左右，而是允许 $z$ 从平面上任意方向、沿任意路径趋近 $z_0$；极限存在意味着所有这些趋近方式都给出同一个 $A$。极限若存在必唯一：若 $A\ne B$，取 $\varepsilon=|A-B|/3$，在公共的 $\delta$ 内用三角不等式即得矛盾。

写 $f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)$、$A=a+ib$，则 $$\begin{aligned}\lim_{z\to z_0}f(z)=A\iff{}&\lim_{(x,y)\to(x_0,y_0)}u(x,y)=a\\&\text{且}\ \lim_{(x,y)\to(x_0,y_0)}v(x,y)=b.\end{aligned}$$ 事实上，由 $|u-a|\le|f-A|$、$|v-b|\le|f-A|$ 可从复极限推出两个实极限；反过来由 $$|f-A|\le|u-a|+|v-b|$$ 可从两个实极限推出复极限。这条等价性把复极限问题化为二元实函数的二重极限问题。

判断极限不存在，只需找到两条趋近路径给出不同结果。例如 $f(z)= ar z/z$（$z
e0$）在 $z	o0$ 时：沿实轴 $z=x
e0$，$f=x/x=1$；沿虚轴 $z=iy
e0$，$f=(-iy)/(iy)=-1$。两条路径的极限不同，故 $\lim_{z	o0} ar z/z$ 不存在。更一般地，令 $z=re^{i\varphi}$，则 $f=e^{-2i\varphi}$，结果随方向角 $\varphi$ 改变。注意：验证有限条路径只能用来否定极限；要证明存在，必须对所有路径一致地验证 $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ 条件。

复极限满足与实极限相同的四则运算法则：若 $\lim f=F$、$\lim g=G$，则 $\lim(f\pm g)=F\pm G$、$\lim(fg)=FG$，且当 $G\ne0$ 时 $\lim(f/g)=F/G$。多项式在整个复平面连续，有理函数在分母不为零处连续。例如 $$\lim_{z\to i}\frac{z^2+1}{z-i}=\lim_{z\to i}\frac{(z-i)(z+i)}{z-i}=\lim_{z\to i}(z+i)=2i,$$ 其中约分只在 $z\ne i$ 时进行，而极限恰好与 $z=i$ 处的取值无关。

若 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 的某邻域内有定义，且 $\lim_{z\to z_0}f(z)=f(z_0)$，则称 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 连续。由第 2 步，$f$ 在 $z_0$ 连续当且仅当 $u,v$ 在 $(x_0,y_0)$ 连续。连续函数的和、差、积、商（分母非零）与复合仍连续；$z$、$\bar z$、$|z|$ 以及多项式处处连续，有理函数在其定义域内连续。连续只要求极限等于函数值，不要求可导。

用定义验证一个正例：证明 $\lim_{z\to0}z^2=0$。对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，取 $\delta=\sqrt\varepsilon$；当 $0<|z|<\delta$ 时，$|z^2-0|=|z|^2<\delta^2=\varepsilon$，故极限为 $0$。若改用极坐标 $z=re^{i\theta}$，要证明极限为 $0$，需给出不依赖 $\theta$ 的估计，例如 $|z^2|=r^2\to0$；若沿不同固定方向 $\theta$ 令 $r\to0$ 得到不同的极限值，则极限不存在；仅表达式中出现 $\theta$ 不足以否定极限，需给出不依赖 $\theta$ 的一致估计。方向一致性与 $\theta$ 的一致性，是复极限区别于实极限的关键。
en: Let $f$ be defined in a punctured neighbourhood of $z_0$. If there is a complex number $A$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ with $|f(z)-A|<\varepsilon$ whenever $0<|z-z_0|<\delta$, then $$\lim_{z\to z_0}f(z)=A.$$ Unlike the real case, $0<|z-z_0|<\delta$ does not distinguish left from right: $z$ may approach $z_0$ from any direction and along any path, and the limit exists only if all these approaches give the same $A$. A limit, if it exists, is unique: if $A\ne B$, take $\varepsilon=|A-B|/3$ and use the triangle inequality on a common $\delta$ to obtain a contradiction.

Write $f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)$ and $A=a+ib$. Then $$\begin{aligned}\lim_{z\to z_0}f(z)=A\iff{}&\lim_{(x,y)\to(x_0,y_0)}u(x,y)=a\\&\text{and}\ \lim_{(x,y)\to(x_0,y_0)}v(x,y)=b.\end{aligned}$$ Indeed, $|u-a|\le|f-A|$ and $|v-b|\le|f-A|$ give the implication from the complex limit to the two real limits; conversely, $$|f-A|\le|u-a|+|v-b|$$ gives the reverse implication. This equivalence reduces complex limits to double limits of real functions of two variables.

To show that a limit fails to exist, it suffices to find two paths with different limits. For example, for $f(z)= ar z/z$ ($z
e0$) as $z	o0$: along the real axis $z=x
e0$, $f=x/x=1$; along the imaginary axis $z=iy
e0$, $f=(-iy)/(iy)=-1$. The two limits differ, so $\lim_{z	o0} ar z/z$ does not exist. More generally, with $z=re^{i\varphi}$, $f=e^{-2i\varphi}$, which depends on the direction $\varphi$. Note that checking finitely many paths can only disprove a limit; proving existence requires the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition uniformly over all paths.

Complex limits obey the same algebraic rules as real limits: if $\lim f=F$ and $\lim g=G$, then $\lim(f\pm g)=F\pm G$ and $\lim(fg)=FG$; if $G\ne0$, then $\lim(f/g)=F/G$. Polynomials are continuous on the whole plane, and rational functions are continuous wherever the denominator does not vanish. For example, $$\lim_{z\to i}\frac{z^2+1}{z-i}=\lim_{z\to i}\frac{(z-i)(z+i)}{z-i}=\lim_{z\to i}(z+i)=2i,$$ where the cancellation is valid only for $z\ne i$, while the limit is independent of the value at $z=i$.

If $f$ is defined in a neighbourhood of $z_0$ and $\lim_{z\to z_0}f(z)=f(z_0)$, then $f$ is continuous at $z_0$. By Step 2, $f$ is continuous at $z_0$ iff $u$ and $v$ are continuous at $(x_0,y_0)$. Sums, differences, products, quotients (with nonzero denominator) and compositions of continuous functions are continuous; $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|$ and all polynomials are continuous everywhere, and rational functions are continuous on their domains. Continuity requires only that the limit equal the value, not differentiability.

A positive verification from the definition: prove $\lim_{z\to0}z^2=0$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, take $\delta=\sqrt\varepsilon$; if $0<|z|<\delta$, then $|z^2-0|=|z|^2<\delta^2=\varepsilon$, so the limit is $0$. In polar form $z=re^{i\theta}$, proving a limit equals $0$ requires an estimate independent of $\theta$, such as $|z^2|=r^2\to0$; if different fixed directions $\theta$ give different limits as $r\to0$, the limit does not exist; the mere presence of $\theta$ is insufficient—one needs a $\theta$-independent estimate. Uniformity in direction—and in $\theta$—is what distinguishes complex limits from real ones.

zh: 设 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 的某邻域内有定义。若差商极限 $$f'(z_0)=\lim_{\Delta z\to0}\frac{f(z_0+\Delta z)-f(z_0)}{\Delta z}$$ 存在，则称 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 可导（可微）。这里 $\Delta z$ 是复数，必须沿任意方向趋于 $0$ 时极限都相同。例如 $f(z)=z^2$ 时差商为 $2z_0+\Delta z\to2z_0$；而 $f(z)=\bar z$ 时 $$\frac{\overline{\Delta z}}{\Delta z}=e^{-2i\varphi}$$ 随方向角 $\varphi$ 改变，故 $\bar z$ 处处不可导。可导必连续，证明与实情形相同。

若 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 的某个邻域内处处可导，则称 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 解析（全纯）；若在区域 $D$ 内每点解析，则称 $f$ 是 $D$ 内的解析函数。解析强于一点可导：$f(z)=|z|^2$ 在 $z=0$ 可导，因为 $$\frac{|\Delta z|^2}{\Delta z}=\overline{\Delta z}\to0,$$ 但对 $z_0\ne0$，差商为 $z_0\overline{\Delta z}/\Delta z+\bar z_0+\overline{\Delta z}$，第一项随方向改变，故不可导。因此 $|z|^2$ 只在 $z=0$ 可导，处处不解析。区域是开集，所以在区域内「处处可导」与「解析」等价。

设 $f=u+iv$ 在 $z_0=x_0+iy_0$ 可导。分别沿水平方向 $\Delta z=\Delta x$ 与竖直方向 $\Delta z=i\Delta y$ 计算差商，两个极限都必须等于 $f'(z_0)$，比较实部与虚部即得柯西-黎曼方程 $$u_x=v_y,\qquad u_y=-v_x,$$ 其中偏导数都在 $(x_0,y_0)$ 取值。这是可导的必要条件：不满足它的函数必不可导。但仅有 C-R 方程还不够，还需 $u,v$ 在该点可微；反例与完整证明见「柯西-黎曼方程」节点。

充分性：若 $u,v$ 在 $(x_0,y_0)$ 可微且满足 C-R 方程，则 $f=u+iv$ 在 $z_0$ 可导，且 $$f'(z_0)=u_x+iv_x=v_y-iu_y.$$ 证明要点：由可微性，$\Delta u=u_x\Delta x+u_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|)$，$\Delta v=v_x\Delta x+v_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|)$；用 $u_y=-v_x$、$v_y=u_x$ 代入，得 $$\Delta f=(u_x+iv_x)(\Delta x+i\Delta y)+o(|\Delta z|),$$ 除以 $\Delta z$ 即得结论。若 $u,v$ 在区域 $D$ 内有连续一阶偏导且处处满足 C-R 方程，则 $f$ 在 $D$ 内解析。

解析函数对四则运算与复合封闭：若 $f,g$ 在区域 $D$ 内解析，则 $f\pm g$、$fg$ 解析；在 $g(z)\ne0$ 处 $f/g$ 解析；若 $g(D)\subset D'$ 且 $f$ 在 $D'$ 解析，则 $f\circ g$ 解析。常数、$z$ 的多项式、$e^z$、$\sin z$、$\cos z$ 都是整函数（全平面解析），有理函数在分母不为零处解析。这些结论可由导数法则或 C-R 方程逐点验证，例如 $z^2$ 的导数为 $2z$。

解析性带来刚性与几何性质。若 $f$ 在区域 $D$ 内解析且 $f'\equiv0$，则 $u_x=u_y=v_x=v_y=0$；由于 $D$ 连通，$u,v$ 各自为常数，故 $f$ 为常数。进一步，若 $u,v$ 有二阶连续偏导，则由 C-R 方程得 $$u_{xx}+u_{yy}=0,\qquad v_{xx}+v_{yy}=0,$$ 即实部与虚部都是调和函数；在 $f'(z)\ne0$ 处，$u=c$ 与 $v=c$ 两族等值线正交，映射保角。解析函数因此同时具有强烈的代数刚性与鲜明的几何意义。
en: Let $f$ be defined in a neighbourhood of $z_0$. If the difference quotient $$f'(z_0)=\lim_{\Delta z\to0}\frac{f(z_0+\Delta z)-f(z_0)}{\Delta z}$$ has a limit, then $f$ is differentiable at $z_0$, with derivative $f'(z_0)$. Here $\Delta z$ is complex, so the limit must be the same as $\Delta z\to0$ along every direction. For $f(z)=z^2$ the quotient is $2z_0+\Delta z\to2z_0$; for $f(z)=\bar z$ it is $$\frac{\overline{\Delta z}}{\Delta z}=e^{-2i\varphi},$$ which depends on the direction angle $\varphi$, so $\bar z$ is nowhere differentiable. Differentiability implies continuity, by the same proof as in the real case.

If $f$ is differentiable at every point of some neighbourhood of $z_0$, then $f$ is analytic (holomorphic) at $z_0$; if it is analytic at every point of a region $D$, it is an analytic function in $D$. Analyticity is stronger than differentiability at one point: $f(z)=|z|^2$ is differentiable at $z=0$, since $$\frac{|\Delta z|^2}{\Delta z}=\overline{\Delta z}\to0,$$ but for $z_0\ne0$ the quotient is $z_0\overline{\Delta z}/\Delta z+\bar z_0+\overline{\Delta z}$, whose first term depends on the direction, so $f$ is not differentiable there. Hence $|z|^2$ is differentiable only at $z=0$ and analytic nowhere. Since a region is open, differentiability everywhere in a region is equivalent to analyticity there.

Let $f=u+iv$ be differentiable at $z_0=x_0+iy_0$. Computing the difference quotient along the horizontal direction $\Delta z=\Delta x$ and the vertical direction $\Delta z=i\Delta y$, both limits must equal $f'(z_0)$; comparing real and imaginary parts gives the Cauchy–Riemann equations $$u_x=v_y,\qquad u_y=-v_x,$$ with all partials evaluated at $(x_0,y_0)$. This is a necessary condition for differentiability: a function violating it cannot be differentiable. The equations alone are not sufficient; one also needs $u,v$ differentiable at the point. The counterexample and full proof are given in the Cauchy–Riemann node.

Sufficiency: if $u,v$ are differentiable at $(x_0,y_0)$ and satisfy the C-R equations, then $f=u+iv$ is differentiable at $z_0$, and $$f'(z_0)=u_x+iv_x=v_y-iu_y.$$ The proof: differentiability gives $\Delta u=u_x\Delta x+u_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|)$ and $\Delta v=v_x\Delta x+v_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|)$; substituting $u_y=-v_x$ and $v_y=u_x$ yields $$\Delta f=(u_x+iv_x)(\Delta x+i\Delta y)+o(|\Delta z|),$$ and division by $\Delta z$ gives the result. If $u,v$ have continuous first partials in a region $D$ and satisfy the C-R equations throughout $D$, then $f$ is analytic in $D$.

Analytic functions are closed under the four operations and composition: if $f,g$ are analytic in a region $D$, then $f\pm g$ and $fg$ are analytic; $f/g$ is analytic where $g(z)\ne0$; and if $g(D)\subset D'$ and $f$ is analytic on $D'$, then $f\circ g$ is analytic. Constants, polynomials in $z$, $e^z$, $\sin z$ and $\cos z$ are entire (analytic on the whole plane), and rational functions are analytic wherever the denominator does not vanish. These facts follow pointwise from the derivative rules or from the C-R equations; for example, the derivative of $z^2$ is $2z$.

Analyticity imposes rigidity and has geometric consequences. If $f$ is analytic in a region $D$ and $f'\equiv0$, then $u_x=u_y=v_x=v_y=0$; since $D$ is connected, $u$ and $v$ are constant, hence so is $f$. Moreover, when $u,v$ have continuous second partials, the C-R equations give $$u_{xx}+u_{yy}=0,\qquad v_{xx}+v_{yy}=0,$$ so the real and imaginary parts are harmonic. Where $f'(z)\ne0$, the level curves $u=c$ and $v=c$ are orthogonal and the mapping is conformal. Analytic functions therefore combine strong algebraic rigidity with a clear geometric meaning.

再沿竖直方向取 $\Delta z=i\Delta y$（$\Delta y\in\mathbb R$，$\Delta y\to0$）：$$\begin{aligned}\frac{f(z_0+i\Delta y)-f(z_0)}{i\Delta y}&=\frac{\Delta u}{i\Delta y}+i\frac{\Delta v}{i\Delta y}\\&=v_y-iu_y,\end{aligned}$$ 极限为 $v_y(x_0,y_0)-iu_y(x_0,y_0)$。同一导数 $f'(z_0)$ 的实部、虚部必须分别相等，于是 $$u_x=v_y,\qquad u_y=-v_x.$$ 这就是柯西-黎曼方程（C-R 方程），是可导的必要条件。

C-R 方程本身不充分。反例：$$f(z)=\sqrt{|xy|}\quad(z=x+iy),$$ 即 $u=\sqrt{|xy|}$、$v=0$。在原点，沿 $x$ 轴 $u(x,0)=0$，故 $u_x(0,0)=0$；沿 $y$ 轴同理 $u_y(0,0)=0$，于是 $u_x=v_y=0$、$u_y=-v_x=0$，C-R 方程成立。但沿 $y=x$ 且 $x\to0^\pm$，$$\frac{f(z)-f(0)}{z}=\frac{|x|}{x(1+i)}\to\frac{\pm1}{1+i},$$ 两个单侧极限不同，故 $f$ 在 $0$ 不可导。原因正是 $u$ 在原点不可微。

充分性：若 $u,v$ 在 $(x_0,y_0)$ 可微且满足 C-R 方程，则 $f$ 在 $z_0$ 可导，且 $$f'(z_0)=u_x+iv_x=v_y-iu_y.$$ 证明：可微性给出 $$\begin{aligned}\Delta u&=u_x\Delta x+u_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|),\\ \Delta v&=v_x\Delta x+v_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|).\end{aligned}$$ 由 C-R 方程 $u_y=-v_x$、$v_y=u_x$，所以 $$\begin{aligned}\Delta f&=(u_x+iv_x)\Delta x+(-v_x+iu_x)\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|)\\&=(u_x+iv_x)(\Delta x+i\Delta y)+o(|\Delta z|).\end{aligned}$$ 除以 $\Delta z=\Delta x+i\Delta y$，令 $\Delta z\to0$ 即得结论。

First take the horizontal direction $\Delta z=\Delta x$ with $\Delta x\in\mathbb R$, $\Delta x\to0$: $$\begin{aligned}\frac{f(z_0+\Delta x)-f(z_0)}{\Delta x}&=\frac{\Delta u}{\Delta x}+i\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta x}\\&\to u_x(x_0,y_0)+iv_x(x_0,y_0).\end{aligned}$$ Since the difference-quotient limit exists, its real and imaginary parts converge separately; hence $u_x,v_x$ exist and $f'(z_0)=u_x+iv_x$.

Next take the vertical direction $\Delta z=i\Delta y$ with $\Delta y\in\mathbb R$, $\Delta y\to0$: $$\begin{aligned}\frac{f(z_0+i\Delta y)-f(z_0)}{i\Delta y}&=\frac{\Delta u}{i\Delta y}+i\frac{\Delta v}{i\Delta y}\\&=v_y-iu_y,\end{aligned}$$ with limit $v_y(x_0,y_0)-iu_y(x_0,y_0)$. The real and imaginary parts of the same derivative $f'(z_0)$ must agree, so $$u_x=v_y,\qquad u_y=-v_x.$$ These are the Cauchy–Riemann equations (C-R equations), a necessary condition for differentiability.

The C-R equations alone are not sufficient. Counterexample: $$f(z)=\sqrt{|xy|}\quad(z=x+iy),$$ i.e. $u=\sqrt{|xy|}$ and $v=0$. At the origin, $u(x,0)=0$ along the $x$-axis, so $u_x(0,0)=0$; similarly $u_y(0,0)=0$ along the $y$-axis. Hence $u_x=v_y=0$ and $u_y=-v_x=0$, so the C-R equations hold. But along $y=x$ with $x\to0^\pm$, $$\frac{f(z)-f(0)}{z}=\frac{|x|}{x(1+i)}\to\frac{\pm1}{1+i},$$ two different one-sided limits; hence $f$ is not differentiable at $0$. The reason is precisely that $u$ is not differentiable at the origin.

Sufficiency: if $u,v$ are differentiable at $(x_0,y_0)$ and satisfy the C-R equations, then $f$ is differentiable at $z_0$, and $$f'(z_0)=u_x+iv_x=v_y-iu_y.$$ Proof: differentiability gives $$\begin{aligned}\Delta u&=u_x\Delta x+u_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|),\\ \Delta v&=v_x\Delta x+v_y\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|).\end{aligned}$$ Using $u_y=-v_x$ and $v_y=u_x$, $$\begin{aligned}\Delta f&=(u_x+iv_x)\Delta x+(-v_x+iu_x)\Delta y+o(|\Delta z|)\\&=(u_x+iv_x)(\Delta x+i\Delta y)+o(|\Delta z|).\end{aligned}$$ Dividing by $\Delta z=\Delta x+i\Delta y$ and letting $\Delta z\to0$ proves the claim.

Region version (the usual form): if $u,v$ have continuous first partial derivatives in a region $D$ and satisfy $u_x=v_y$, $u_y=-v_x$ throughout $D$, then $f=u+iv$ is analytic in $D$, with $f'=u_x+iv_x$. Continuity ensures that $u,v$ are differentiable, so Step 4 applies. Example: $f(z)=e^z=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$, so $u=e^x\cos y$ and $v=e^x\sin y$. Then $$u_x=e^x\cos y=v_y,\qquad u_y=-e^x\sin y=-v_x,$$ and the partials are continuous; hence $e^z$ is entire and $f'(z)=u_x+iv_x=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)=e^z$.
